newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dollar digs in fearing rate bombshell.
newsitem.headline: Australian dollar digs in fearing rate bombshell.

text.p: The Australian dollar suffered another session of hesitation Thursday as support proved just as stubborn as resistance in trade that was very much two-way.

Sellers were encouraged by speculation the Reserve Bank would yet cut domestic interest rates following favourable inflation and wages news this week. But bears were met by solid demand at US$0.7740 and the market mood was made extra cautious by talk an Asian name was protecting a large strangle option.
Traders had suspicions about the rumours but felt they were a perfect excuse for the market to do nothing ahead of Friday's national ANZAC Day holiday here.
By 5.00 pm (0700 GMT) the unit had taken a defensive stance at US$0.7756/61 after slipping from an early US$0.7760/65 and US$0.7777/82 late Wednesday, but was up on a US$0.7735 low.

It had now spent more than a week bouncing around in a broad US$0.7690/7795 band and looked set to remain there short-term as the local market squared up for the ANZAC holiday tomorrow and a raft of domestic and U.S. economic data next week.

A break of US$0.7680 or US$0.7820 would end the deadlock and, given the large stops that were believed to be building either side, could easily see a 1/2 cent lunge afterwards with US$0.7630 and US$0.7895 the big technical targets.
On the crosses the dollar recouped early losses and actually added to big gains made Wednesday as funds flowed out of the yen and lower yielding European currencies.
It edged up to 98.00/10 yen from a 97.69 low and 97.92/02 late Wednesday, aided by direct Japanese demand for government bonds and speculation of further dual currency samurai bonds.
NSW TCorp successfully launched the first yen/A$ issue in a while Tuesday and dealers believed a 15 bln yen issue for the Asian Development Bank had been launched by Daiwa on Wednesday.
The A$ also held firm at 1.3326/40 marks having climbed to 1.3320/37 late Wednesday from 1.3204/18 the day before.
The Japanese demand was welcomed by bulls given there had been a widespread expectation the steady contraction of the A$ yield premium over the US$ would see offshore demand dry up.

Yields on one and two-year government bonds were now below their U.S. counterparts, was were rates on six to 12-month money which in turn had taken A$ forward rates to their highest premium in more than a decade.

And the trend was likely to continue with much of the market expecting the Federal Reserve to hike U.S. rates at its May 20 meeting, probably taking the fed funds rate to 5.75 percent against an official rate here of 6.00 percent.
But there was also the chance the Reserve Bank would ease in the next few months, an event which would take Australian official rates below those in the U.S. for the first time since early 1980s.
This week's inflation and wgaes data seemed to open the door for such an easing but analysts felt it would take a marked slowing in the real side data to push the RBA into it.
Figures of importance next week would be Q1 average weekly earnings and March building approvals Thursday, and retail trade for March and the first quarter on Friday.
